title: Translate an immediate separable prime-degree generator to suppress intermediate coefficients
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, and suppose $K$ is complete. Put $F^\circ=\{x\in F:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|$ for $F=K,L$. Suppose $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde K)>0$, $[L:K]=p$ (vector-space dimension), $\Gamma_L=\Gamma_K$ and $\widetilde L=\widetilde K$. Let $\alpha\in L\setminus K$ have separable monic minimal polynomial over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension, def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Set $r=\inf_{c\in K}|\alpha-c|$, and assume explicitly that $r>0$ and this infimum is not attained. There is $c_0\in K$ such that, writing $\beta=\alpha-c_0$, $R=|\beta|>r$ and its monic minimal polynomial [def-weil-polynomial-ring] as $$f(T)=T^p+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}u_iT^i+b,$$ one has $$|u_1|\le r^{p-1},\qquad |u_i|R^i<r^p\quad(2\le i<p),\qquad |p|R^p<r^p.$$ Here $u_i,b\in K$, and $p$ in the absolute value denotes the image of the integer $p$ in $K$. For $p=2$ the middle family of inequalities is empty.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, immediate case of the proof, printed pp. 39–40 (PDF pages 39–40); Proposition 6.1.1, printed p. 36. Read at the source URL; PDF absent from the read clone.

proof.text: The residue characteristic $p$ is prime, and $p\ge2$. For $1\le i<p$, the integer $i$ has nonzero residue, hence $|i|=1$; also $|p|<1$, including $p=0$ in $K$. By degree multiplicativity, $[K(\alpha):K]>1$ divides $p$, so $K(\alpha)=L$. The monic minimal polynomial $f_0$ has degree $p$: division by it identifies $K[\alpha]$ with $K[T]/(f_0)$, with basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{\deg f_0-1}$; multiplication by any nonzero element of the finite-dimensional domain $K[\alpha]$ is injective, hence surjective, so it is a field and equals $K(\alpha)$. Take an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $L$; it is also algebraic over $K$, since algebraic coefficients lie in a finite extension and adjoining a polynomial root is finite. Equip $\Omega$ with the spectral absolute value over the complete field $K$. Uniqueness of the extending absolute value makes its restriction to $L$ the given absolute value.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, separable immediate case, printed pp. 39–40; algebraic-closure norm and prime-degree setup expanded using the cited tools.

proof.text: If a nonzero $h\in K[T]$ has degree $<p$ and $h(z)=0$ in $\Omega$, its monic minimal polynomial divides $h$ by division with remainder, so $n=[K(z):K]\le\deg h<p$. Finite ramification calculus gives $n=efp^a$ for an integer $a\ge0$, and $K(z)$ is complete. Thus $a=0$ and $n=ef$, so the best-approximation lemma applies to $z$. If $|\alpha-z|\le r$, then for every $c\in K$ the strict inequality $|\alpha-c|>r$ and the ultrametric inequality give $|z-c|=|\alpha-c|$. Their infima would both be $r$ and unattained, contrary to best approximation in $K(z)$. Consequently every such root satisfies $|\alpha-z|>r$. Constant nonzero $h$ has no roots.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40: degree bound for closed points of the nonsplit radius-r disc, expanded without Berkovich terminology.

proof.text: For $1\le i<p$ set $h_i=f_0^{(i)}/i!$, with iterated formal derivatives. The factorial is invertible because $|j|=1$ for $1\le j<p$. Each nonzero $h_i$ has degree $\le p-i<p$, and $h_1\ne0$: otherwise $f_0$ could not be coprime to its derivative. Each polynomial has finitely many roots, since factoring off $T-z$ lowers degree. By Step 2 all these roots have distance $>r$ from $\alpha$. Choose $c_*\in K$ so $R_*=|\alpha-c_*|$ is smaller than every one of these finitely many distances. If the list is empty take any $c_*$. The unattained infimum guarantees $R_*>r$. Each listed root $z$ then has $|z-c_*|=|z-\alpha|>R_*$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40: simultaneously shrink the split disc so every nonzero higher derivative is invertible.

proof.text: Factor a nonzero $h_i$ over $\Omega$, successively using algebraic closedness, and write $$h_i(c_*+T)=h_i(c_*)\prod_z\left(1+\frac{T}{c_*-z}\right),$$ counting roots with multiplicity. Every nonconstant coefficient of the product is a finite sum of products of reciprocal root distances, so its absolute value times $R_*^j$ is $<1$ in degree $j>0$. Thus for every $d\in K$ with $|d|\le R_*$ one has $|h_i(c_*+d)-h_i(c_*)|<|h_i(c_*)|$, and in particular $|h_i(c_*+d)|=|h_i(c_*)|$. For a constant $h_i$ this is immediate. If $h_i=0$ all its values vanish. This finite-product calculation is the polynomial case of the split-disc unit criterion in the source.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40: split-disc unit criterion, proved here directly by factoring polynomials and expanding the finite product.

proof.text: For $c\in K$ write $f_c(T)=f_0(T+c)$, the monic minimal polynomial of $\alpha-c$ (translation preserves degree, vanishing and irreducibility). Its coefficient in degree $i<p$ is $h_i(c)$: expand each monomial by the binomial theorem, or differentiate $i$ times and divide by $i!$. Put $a_i=h_i(c_*)$ and $A_i=|a_i|$. Whenever $|\alpha-c|\le R_*$, one has $|c-c_*|\le R_*$, hence Step 4 gives $|h_i(c)|=A_i$ for every $1\le i<p$. Moreover $A_1>0$. Applying the strict coefficient inequality of Step 4 to $h_1(c_*+T)=f_{c_*}\prime(T)$ gives $$A_iR_*^{i-1}<A_1\quad(2\le i<p),$$ because its coefficient of $T^{i-1}$ is $i a_i$ and $|i|=1$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40: higher-derivative coefficient stability and the first-derivative inequalities.

proof.text: For every $c\in K$, the spectral-value formula for the minimal polynomial of $\alpha-c$, together with uniqueness of the extending absolute value, gives $$|h_1(c)|^{1/(p-1)}\le|\alpha-c|.$$ Indeed the left side is the degree-one term in the supremum defining its spectral norm. Take $c$ with $r<|\alpha-c|\le R_*$ approaching $r$. Step 5 makes $|h_1(c)|=A_1$ throughout this family; hence $A_1\le r^{p-1}$. For $2\le i<p$, Step 5 then yields $$A_i<\frac{A_1}{R_*^{i-1}}\le\frac{r^{p-1}}{R_*^{i-1}}<r^{p-i}.$$ Thus $A_ir^i<r^p$, strictly, for every intermediate index.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40: bound on the linear coefficient and limiting shrink; the cited spectral-norm formula supplies the irreducible-polynomial estimate attributed there to BGR 3.2.4/3.

proof.text: All the finitely many inequalities $A_i r^i<r^p$ for $2\le i<p$ are strict, and $|p|r^p<r^p$ since $r>0$ and $|p|<1$. Continuity of the real powers lets us choose $\rho$ with $r<\rho<R_*$ such that $A_i\rho^i<r^p$ for all those indices and $|p|\rho^p<r^p$. Choose $c_0\in K$ with $R=|\alpha-c_0|<\rho$; nonattainment gives $R>r$. Step 5 identifies the coefficients of $f_{c_0}$ as $u_i=h_i(c_0)$ with $|u_i|=A_i$, while Step 6 gives $|u_1|\le r^{p-1}$. Monotonicity gives $|u_i|R^i<r^p$ and $|p|R^p<r^p$. For $p=2$ the intermediate-index family is empty and the same choice uses only the last inequality. In characteristic $p$, $|p|=0$, so that inequality holds automatically.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40: additional shrinking immediately before setting a=-a_1.
